scope: Step 6 moves every generated slot body and every chain-owned hand body to the port class of its retail owner: the entity chain's bodies onto FElysiumEntity, FElysiumAnimating, the new FElysiumAnimatingOverlay and FElysiumFlex, and FElysiumCombatCharacter; the NPC layers' stay on FElysiumNpcBase / FElysiumNpc. Stubs keep counting and name their retail owner; one dead stub is deleted; the eight entity-method candidates get their audited dispositions; obsolete tables whose last consumer is a test are retired; kernel_shape --unported pins the live unported rule set; the census tests check owners. The ten deferred classes stay listed.

rules.owner: A body's owner is the most-base class of the retail chain CBaseEntity -> CBaseToggle -> CBaseAnimating -> CBaseAnimatingOverlay -> CBaseFlex -> CBaseCombatCharacter -> CAI_BaseNPC -> CAI_BaseNPCTroika whose primary vtable holds the same (thunk-resolved) pointer at that slot. Ghidra's namespace label is not an owner (95 CBaseEntity-held bodies are labelled CAISound::).
rules.declaration: A slot's virtual is declared on the port class of its introducer (the most-base table that holds the slot) with that class's own body; every more-derived chain class whose table changes the pointer overrides it. No introducer body in this chain is _purecall or missing.
rules.toggle: The port has no CBaseToggle node (gen_kernel_bindings' stated divergence). CBaseToggle's own bodies (slots 5, 31, 82, 108-110, 133, 135, 152) go on FElysiumAnimating, the nearest port class below it; where CBaseAnimating refills the slot, its body wins there.
rules.new_chain_rows: 102 rows are chain classes' own bodies the NPC does not run (an introducer or intermediate body under a more-derived owner). They are emitted as stubs of that body on its class, never as behaviour. Nothing calls them on a non-NPC receiver today; a stub fired on a new receiver class is a behaviour delta that test_delta reports.
rules.hand_closure: A chain-owned hand body moves with the members it reaches (moves-step6.tsv): a member follows its most-base user. A member that stands for an NPC-layer word (the shape map's CAI_BaseNPC band) blocks the move; a carrier that stands for a chain word moves up with its word. A retail chain body's +0x98 m_pBaseNPCTroika arm stays an AsNpc() arm (FireBullets 185, FInAimCone 364/365), never a cast.
rules.requalify: A qualified direct call FElysiumNpcBase::X to a body that moves is requalified to its new owner.
rules.save_order: Moved words keep their existing Serialize lines (the NPC base still writes them); save files are disposable (CLAUDE.md).
rules.name_hazard: FElysiumNpcBase is a prefix of FElysiumNpcBaseBoss, FElysiumAnimating a prefix of FElysiumAnimatingOverlay: every codemod and checker match uses word boundaries.
rules.collisions: gen_kernel_shape's reserved-name scan covers every class that derives from the chain across Source/ (the player, items, props, makers, directors and the rest of the ~50 FElysiumEntity subclasses): a same-name member there fails generation until SLOT_PORT_MAP resolves it.

gen_kernel_shape's widened scan (every class deriving from the chain below the NPC line) found eight slot names a subclass also declares. Each is a SLOT_PORT_MAP `accepted` row: 66/67 FElysiumWeapon::Hide/Unhide(FElysiumCombatCharacter*), 86/123 FElysiumCameraCinematic's ShouldTransmit/DrawDebugGeometryOverlays, 107 the deferred maker's ParseMapData(const FString&) (retail CNPCMaker overrides slot 107; the maker fold makes it the override), 133 FElysiumMoverBase::MoveDone (same signature: it becomes the override, retail's shape), 153 FElysiumMoverBase::IsMoving() const and 158 FElysiumPlayer::IsAlive() const (hides by const). Nothing dispatches the hidden forms; the compiler reports each as C4263/C4264. A function-local FName in FElysiumGameSign was a false positive; the scan now reads class-scope lines only.

FElysiumNpcFlags carried m_iIsOblivious (+0x5bb4) and m_bfNPCFrenziedFlags (+0x5b84), both CAI_BaseNPC words in the census, beside the two CBaseCombatCharacter flag words, and 6d moved the aggregate whole to FElysiumCombatCharacter. RESOLVED in 6r: both words are FElysiumNpcBase members (ObliviousCount, FrenziedWord) with their writers (AddOblivious/RemoveOblivious, the grapple pair, SetFrenziedWord) and readers; the shape map binds them as members and gen_kernel_bindings emits their SAVE rows, so FElysiumNpcFlags::Serialize writes only the two flag words. FElysiumNpcFlags::ApplyScheduleChangeMasks answers whether MADE_OBLIVIOUS survived the masks and the runner calls RemoveOblivious (0x102a0a19..0x102a0a45, same order). The trace row keeps its text (FElysiumNpcBase::DescribeNpcFlags). m_bfNPCStateFlags (+0x5b64) has no storage (derived), so only its table stays with the flag vocabulary.

CBaseEntity::IsAlive 0x100b4dc0 reads m_lifeState (+0x200). The port has no such word: it spells alive as neither the death-transaction latch (bDeathReported, on the combat character) nor Kill's bDead stands. On the entity the body reads the latch through AsCombatCharacter(); an entity that is not a combat character has only bDead.

kernel_shape --unported pins 987 live rules the port does not carry: 59 generated stubs with a rule/present/mechanism verdict, 201 bodies of the ten deferred classes, and 727 species bodies at slots their port class (or a species ancestor) does not override. Dead classes and the lifetime slot are excluded. The step-3 matrix's 161 residue rows are its dispatch-scope subset; story 8's pass R counted the rule rows of its bands. The set must only fall.

6b declared FElysiumAnimatingOverlay and FElysiumFlex in ElysiumPlayer.h. .claude/rules/cpp.md says a new class never lands in an existing multi-class file; the rule-conformant layout needs FElysiumAnimating moved verbatim into its own header first (the combat character needs the two new classes complete, so they cannot be included from a header that itself needs ElysiumPlayer.h). Recorded as an open follow-up for the owner. RESOLVED in 6r: FElysiumAnimating moved verbatim to ElysiumAnimating.h in its own commit (bdcfc197, full gate, empty delta), then the two chain classes got ElysiumAnimatingOverlay.h and ElysiumFlex.h.

The unported pin loses CAI_BaseNPC 580 (implemented).

0x1032dde0 had no overlay row, so kernel_shape --unported could not list it. 6r adds a `rule` row (band 19-29, layer 22) whose observable is the species schedules that call slot 388: CNPC_VMingXiao Spawn 0x103927a0, StartTask 0x10392d80, RunTask 0x10393930, PreSelectSchedule 0x10394120 and CNPC_VBach::StartTask 0x103645a0. The pin gains CBaseCombatCharacter 388 (explained here) and stays at 987 with slot 580's removal.

Plan 6h's census tests are C++: NpcKernelShape.SlotOwners (every generated row is declared on its own class, compiler-checked through TDeclaredOn; its retail owner is the class's node, which is the stub's owner prefix; override exactly when a base declares the slot; every generated Troika census row is a row of its owner's table), NpcKernelShape.FieldOwners (shape-map member words live on the port class of their declaring layer, with m_pSenses +0x5cdc the one listed transitional home until fold 9; every census word the descriptor chain binds is bound on its own layer's descriptor), NpcKernelClass.RegistryMatchesFactories (the registry's NPC line builds exactly the 45 classnames; the ten deferred classes listed and off the NPC line).

Plan 6c's per-owner default probes: each port class's generated slot table carries a probe for every default row, typed to that class, and NpcKernelSlots.Defaults calls it on a bare receiver of the class (entity, animating, overlay, flex, combat character), a base-only NPC and a Troika NPC. ShadowedSlotDefaults and its qualified calls, and NpcKernelSlots.ShadowedDefaults, are gone. The census digest is unchanged (the probe tables were never in the row stream).

The step-3 static dispatch gate (kernel_migration_step3.gate_sites) scans non-generated source only, but its GENERATED set still named the pre-rename ElysiumNpcKernelSlots.* files. 6r's slot tables name each slot by member pointer (&FElysiumNpc::X, 169 in ElysiumNpcSlots.cpp) so the compiler can prove the declaring class, which the gate counted as member-pointer dispatch. GENERATED now also names the per-owner Elysium<Class>Slots.{cpp,inl}; no surviving site of any step lies in them, so the older trees' results are unchanged.
